ideology: Military continuity, strict resource rationing, absolute martial law
origin_story: Formed from surviving remnants of the regional armed forces command structure. Colonel Voss assumed command at Bunker Sigma-7 within 72 hours of the Exchange. His first order: 'Civilian dependents will contribute labor or food to the defense effort.' His second: 'Deserters will be shot.' They view all non-military survivors as civilian dependents who must earn their place through labor or combat service.
key_beliefs: Civilization is maintained by supply chains and ammunition counts
Democracy is a luxury of peacetime
Every mouth must earn its rations through labor or combat service
The chain of command is sacred — orders are not debated, they are executed
dialogue_style: Formal, terse, military acronyms, cold operational efficiency
signature_quote: Civilization isn't built on sympathy; it's maintained by supply chains and ammunition counts.

ideology: Local democracy, resource sharing, mutual defense, civilian autonomy
origin_story: A coalition of pre-war farmers, miners, teachers, and tradespeople who banded together when both raider gangs and Garrison conscription units threatened their communities. Founded by a farmer named Delacroix with 47 members and 12 rifles. They hold weekly council meetings in the old Grange Hall, lit by salvaged oil lamps. Every member — regardless of age, gender, or pre-war status — gets one vote.
key_beliefs: If we turn into monsters just to survive, the war already won
Everyone gets a vote and everyone gets a share
The old world ended — we decide what replaces it
A community that abandons its weakest has already lost
dialogue_style: Informal, warm, pragmatic, weary but determined
signature_quote: If we turn into monsters just to survive the fallout, then the war already won.

display_name: The Cult of the Ash Sign
ideology: Apocalyptic purification, radiation worship, ascetic martyrdom
origin_story: A fanatical religious movement that arose in the highest fallout zones — areas too lethal for military patrols. Their prophet, known only as The Vessel, emerged from the ruins of a destroyed reactor unscathed — or so they claim. They believe the nuclear exchange was a divine purging of a corrupt world and view radiation sickness as a spiritual ordeal that cleanses the soul. Members willingly expose themselves to low-level radiation as acts of devotion.
key_beliefs: The nuclear fire was divine judgment on a corrupt world
Radiation is the breath of the new god — breathe it and be cleansed
Death by fallout is not death; it is ascension to the Clear World
The old world's lies were burned away — only truth remains in the ash
dialogue_style: Arcane, rhythmic, serene, unsettlingly peaceful amidst horror
signature_quote: Do not fear the glow, child. The fire burned away the old world's lies. Drink the ash and be renewed.

ideology: Mercenary opportunism, trade control, survival of the fittest
origin_story: A loose syndicate of armed scavengers, former convicts, and ex-mercenaries who control key highway bottlenecks, fuel depots, and river crossings. They have no loyalty beyond the contract. Their leader, The Tollman, rose to power by being the only person who knew the bridge demolition codes after the Exchange. He charges passage in blood or bullets — literal or metaphorical.
key_beliefs: Clean water costs blood or bullets — pick which you're paying with
Loyalty is a tradable commodity, like diesel or antibiotics
The strong don't survive because they're strong — they survive because they're useful
A contract is sacred; everything else is negotiable
dialogue_style: Rough, cynical, transactional, threatening but honest
signature_quote: Clean water costs blood or bullets. Pick which one you're paying with today.
